criteria.criterion: SoldBackfillPlanner retains the successfully parsed ItemPageListing (which already carries RawJson) for each resolved listing, exposed after collection via PriceBandCollectionSummary/SearchCollectionResult, bounded by the existing Scrape:MaxBackfillItemPageFetches budget, and safe under #62's concurrent bands.
criteria.plannedImplementation: SoldBackfillPlanner gained a ConcurrentDictionary<string, ItemPageListing> _resolvedDetails, written in ResolveDate only when FetchDetail returns a non-null parsed page (before the DateLookup is built), keyed by the same listing.ListingId already used as the _dateCache key. Exposed as internal IReadOnlyDictionary<string, ItemPageListing> ResolvedDetails. Because DateOf caches the in-flight Task per listing id, ResolveDate runs at most once per unique listing regardless of how many concurrent bands ask for it, so at most one dictionary entry is ever written per listing and the dictionary can never exceed the number of unique successful fetches, itself capped by _maxItemPageFetches (Scrape:MaxBackfillItemPageFetches). PriceBandCollectionRun.Execute reads backfill.ResolvedDetails only after PriceBandWorkerPool.RunAsync's Task.WhenAll over all concurrent band workers has completed, so the read happens with no bands still writing -- no new locking was needed. PriceBandCollectionSummary.BackfillDetails and SearchCollectionResult.BackfilledDetails carry it out to ScrapeRunService.

SearchPageServiceTests.Should_expose_backfill_resolved_item_pages_for_the_run_to_persist drives a full Mercari band search with CollectSold true and asserts SearchCollectionResult.BackfilledDetails carries the resolved detail keyed by ListingId. criteria.criterion: After the search results are stored, the retained backfill details are persisted through the same ItemDetailStore path the detail phase uses (description, sale date, segmentation fields, sellers, raw JSON identical), those listings are marked detailed so ItemDetailFetchService skips them, and items whose parse failed or resolved as unresolved stay eligible for the normal detail phase.
criteria.plannedImplementation: IItemDetailStore.GetListingEntityIds(jobId, listingIds, ct) is a read-only lookup (no writes, no parallel save path) resolving already-upserted listing rows to entity ids. IItemDetailFetchService.ApplyBackfilledDetails(jobId, detailsByListingId, ct) resolves those entity ids and then calls the pre-existing IItemDetailStore.ApplyItemDetail(entityId, detail, ct) once per match -- the identical method ItemDetailFetchService.FetchDetail already calls for freshly fetched pages -- so ApplyDetailFields, ApplySegmentationDetailFields, SellerUpserter.Apply, and UpsertItemDetailRawData all run exactly as they do in the normal detail phase, and ApplyItemDetail's own listing.DetailFetchedUtc = DateTime.UtcNow stamp is what later excludes the listing from GetListingsNeedingDetail's `l.DetailFetchedUtc == null` filter -- no new selection logic was added. ScrapeRunService.Run calls ApplyBackfilledDetails right after UpsertListings and before FetchDetails. Listings the planner could not resolve are never added to SoldBackfillPlanner.ResolvedDetails (see scope-1), so they never appear in detailsByListingId and are left with DetailFetchedUtc still null, keeping them eligible for the ordinary FetchDetails pass.

ItemDetailStoreTests.Should_map_listing_ids_to_entity_ids_for_only_the_matching_job_and_requested_ids (real SQLite) proves the lookup is scoped to the given job and only returns requested, existing ids. ScrapeRunServiceTests.Should_apply_backfilled_details_before_fetching_the_remaining_detail_targets proves ScrapeRunService calls ApplyBackfilledDetails before FetchDetails (Received.InOrder), and Should_not_call_apply_backfilled_details_when_the_search_found_nothing_to_backfill proves it is skipped when there is nothing to apply.
